new.title: Look into the Verdon canyon from Point Sublime
new.desc: The Belvédère du Point Sublime overlooks the mouth of the Gorges du Verdon from the right bank, below Rougon at about 785 m. Legend says Samson split the mountain here to save Delilah.
new.tip: Free viewpoint, about 10 minutes from the car park by the Auberge du Point Sublime; parking is paid in season. Morning light is best.
new.q: Belvédère du Point Sublime, route de Rougon, Rougon

new.title: Wander the hilltop village of Rougon
new.desc: Rougon is a tiny village of about 120 residents perched above the Samson corridor and Point Sublime. A resident vulture colony nests in the cliffs and the skies are protected from light pollution.
new.tip: Reached only by road via the D17, about 1 km above Point Sublime. Bring binoculars for the vultures.
new.q: Village de Rougon, Rougon

new.title: Climb 262 steps to Notre-Dame de Beauvoir
new.desc: This chapel hangs on the cliff above Moustiers-Sainte-Marie and has been a pilgrimage site since the 12th century. It mixes Romanesque and Gothic work and has been a listed monument since 1921.
new.tip: Free; allow 15 to 20 minutes up the stone staircase. The view over the Maire valley and Valensole plateau is best late afternoon.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame de Beauvoir, Moustiers-Sainte-Marie

new.title: Visit the gardens and museum of Salagon priory
new.desc: Salagon in Mane combines a 12th-century Romanesque priory church with stained glass by Aurélie Nemours, a Renaissance residence and the ethnological museum of Haute-Provence. Its ethnobotanical gardens carry the Jardin remarquable label.
new.tip: Admission is around 6 euros; closed Tuesdays outside school holidays. The site is on the N100, about 3 km south of Forcalquier.
new.q: Salagon, musée et jardins, Mane

new.title: Step inside the Rotonde of Simiane
new.desc: The Rotonde is the 12th-century keep of the Agoult-Simiane castle, hexagonal outside and twelve-sided inside. Its dome carries twelve carved capitals with human masks, and it was restored in 1875.
new.tip: Visit in summer for the village atmosphere and the lavender around the hill; the acoustics inside are remarkable. Park below and walk up.
new.q: Château de Simiane et sa Rotonde, 1 Rue du Château, Simiane-la-Rotonde

new.title: Tour the Citadel of Sisteron
new.desc: This fortress above the Durance guarded the Provence-Dauphiné crossing and is part of the Vauban network. It is open from March to November.
new.tip: Allow about two hours; there are many steps. Summer sunset guided visits need booking.
new.q: Citadelle de Sisteron, Montée de la Citadelle, Sisteron

new.title: See the four Roman columns and baptistery of Riez
new.desc: Four granite columns with white marble Corinthian capitals are the remains of a Roman temple at Riez, probably of Apollo. Nearby stands the early Christian baptistery, one of the few of its age left in Provence, square outside and octagonal within.
new.tip: The columns are free to see by the Colostre; the baptistery is often locked, so check with the tourist office.
new.q: Colonnes romaines, Riez

new.title: Walk up to Notre-Dame du Roc above Castellane
new.desc: The chapel crowns the rock over Castellane on the site of a Mercedarian convent founded in 1663. It was rebuilt after damage in 1590 and gained its present look in the 19th century.
new.tip: Free and open daily; about 30 minutes on foot from the town centre. The view covers the Verdon valley.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame du Roc, Castellane

new.title: Admire the Romanesque mosaic of Ganagobie priory
new.desc: Ganagobie priory sits on a plateau above the Durance. Its church holds a mosaic of about 1124 to 1130, around 72 square metres, with a rider slaying a dragon, found in the late 19th century.
new.tip: Monks still live here, so visits are limited to set hours; check beforehand and dress modestly.
new.q: Prieuré Notre-Dame de Ganagobie, Ganagobie

new.title: Visit the Caurres battery of Fort de Tournoux
new.desc: Fort de Tournoux was built from 1843 to guard the Ubaye valley against invasion from Italy and is a listed monument. Guided tours cover its upper section, the Caurres battery.
new.tip: Tours run by Ubaye Tourisme in summer, about 3 hours with a 3 km walk; book ahead.
new.q: Fort de Tournoux, Batterie des Caurres, La Condamine-Châtelard

new.title: Study the ammonite slab north of Digne
new.desc: The Dalle à ammonites holds over 1,550 ammonites on about 320 square metres of inclined rock, dating from the Sinemurian. It is part of the Haute-Provence geological reserve created in 1984.
new.tip: Free and open all year, 1.5 km north of Digne on the road to Barles, beside the road.
new.q: Dalle à ammonites, route de Barles, Digne-les-Bains

new.title: Climb to the octagonal chapel above Forcalquier
new.desc: Notre-Dame de Provence crowns the hill where the counts of Forcalquier had their castle, destroyed in 1601. The neo-Byzantine chapel of 1875 has statues of medieval musicians and a hand-played carillon.
new.tip: Free access to the site; the chapel is open afternoons. The 360 degree view is best near sunset.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame de Provence, Citadelle, Forcalquier

new.title: Browse 120,000 books at Le Bleuet in Banon
new.desc: Le Bleuet is a bookshop on Place Saint-Just, founded in 1990 and now one of the largest rural bookshops in France. It spreads over four floors and hosts readings and exhibitions.
new.tip: Open 10:00 to 19:00, later in July and August. Combine with Banon's Tuesday market.
new.q: Librairie Le Bleuet, Place Saint-Just, Banon

new.title: Taste Banon AOP goat cheese at La Fromagerie de Banon
new.desc: Banon AOP is a raw whole-milk goat cheese ripened in chestnut leaves tied with raffia. The family farm dairy on the D51 south of the village sells it directly.
new.tip: Ask about tastings; buy it wrapped in leaves. The village market is Tuesday morning.
new.q: La Fromagerie de Banon, route de Carniol, Banon

new.title: Dine on garden vegetables at La Bastide de Moustiers
new.desc: Alain Ducasse's Provençal inn opened in 1994 and holds a Michelin star. The menu follows the vegetable garden and market, and the kitchen has passed to chef Valentin Fuchs.
new.tip: Expect around 95 euros per person; reserve ahead. Chemin de Quinson, a short drive from the village.
new.q: La Bastide de Moustiers, 511 Chemin de Quinson, Moustiers-Sainte-Marie

new.title: Order pieds et paquets at La Treille Muscate
new.desc: La Treille Muscate on Place de l'Église has cooked Provençal dishes since 1999 and was selected in the 2025 Gault&Millau guide. Pieds et paquets, tripe parcels, is its regional classic alongside confit rabbit and polenta.
new.tip: Reviews are mixed, so book and check recent menus. Terrace seating on the square in summer.
new.q: La Treille Muscate, Place de l'Église, Moustiers-Sainte-Marie

new.title: Eat pieds paquets facing the Sisteron citadel
new.desc: Restaurant Le Cours specialises in Sisteron lamb and pieds paquets, served as a warm salad with gribiche sauce. It also does Provençal daube with polenta.
new.tip: Open for lunch and dinner including Sundays; the summer terrace looks up to the citadel.
new.q: Restaurant Le Cours, 2 Allée de Verdun, Sisteron

new.title: Try praline brioche at Maison Padiou in Barcelonnette
new.desc: Maison Padiou is run by master pastry chef and chocolatier Nicolas Padiou. Its specialities are praline brioches, feuilletine and house ice cream, with a tea room next door.
new.tip: Closed Mondays, Sunday morning only. 47 rue Manuel.
new.q: Maison Padiou, 47 rue Manuel, Barcelonnette

new.title: Sample liqueurs at Distilleries et Domaines de Provence
new.desc: This Forcalquier firm runs a tasting room and small museum on Avenue Saint-Promasse, showing Provençal liqueurs, pastis and essences. Tasting is described as free.
new.tip: Closed Sundays; check opening hours. Pair with the Monday market.
new.q: Distilleries et Domaines de Provence, Avenue Saint-Promasse, Forcalquier

new.title: Finish with lavender-honey ice cream in La Palud
new.desc: Restaurant des Gorges du Verdon on chemin de Boulogne serves fresh Provençal cooking. Its lavender, vanilla and honey ice cream is highlighted by the tourist office.
new.tip: Evening service from 19:00; reservations taken.
new.q: Restaurant des Gorges du Verdon, chemin de Boulogne, La Palud-sur-Verdon

new.title: Eat homemade dishes at Cocotte in Pierrerue
new.desc: Cocotte is a Bistrot de Pays run by a chef-chocolatier-pastry cook and a wine lover, about 5 km from Forcalquier. Everything is homemade, fresh and local.
new.tip: Open Friday and Saturday lunch and dinner only; closed Wednesday and Sunday. Book.
new.q: Cocotte, Bistrot de Pays, Pierrerue

new.title: Buy lavender honey from Lavande Bio Bérenger
new.desc: This organic Valensole producer sells lavender honey and products in a town shop, at markets and from a cabin on the Manosque road, with tastings in bloom season.
new.tip: Best in late June and July when the cabin is open.
new.q: Lavande Bio Bérenger, 4 Rue Albert Richaud, Valensole

new.title: Hike the Blanc-Martel trail through the Verdon gorge
new.desc: This 15 to 16 km one-way route follows the GR4 from the Chalet de la Maline to Point Sublime along the river. It has tunnels and ladders and takes 6 to 7 hours.
new.tip: Shuttle from La Palud at 8:30, return from Point Sublime at 16:00 (check 2026 dates). Carry 3 L of water and a torch.
new.q: Chalet de la Maline (CAF), Sentier Blanc-Martel, La Palud-sur-Verdon

new.title: Ride the Route des Crêtes loop above the Verdon
new.desc: The Route des Crêtes is a 24 km panoramic road with 14 viewpoints, including Dent d'Aire over 700 m above the river. Cyclists can ride it with or without electric assistance.
new.tip: Ride clockwise. Tunnel works close the one-way section on weekdays 8:00 to 17:30; check.
new.q: La Palud-sur-Verdon, Route des Crêtes

new.title: Paddle or pedal on Lac de Sainte-Croix
new.desc: The Sainte-Croix-du-Verdon nautical base rents pedal boats, canoes, kayaks and stand-up paddles, and the village has a supervised beach. The lake season runs April to October.
new.tip: Go early on summer days. Book if you want to paddle to the gorge mouth.
new.q: Base nautique, Plage de Sainte-Croix-du-Verdon

new.title: Walk the Sentier des Pénitents at Les Mées
new.desc: This loop of about 4.5 km, around two hours, follows the ridge by the Pénitents rocks above the Durance. A rockfall in December 2019 hit houses, so stay on marked paths.
new.tip: Start from the tourist office or the large car park on the D4. Easy but exposed.
new.q: Rocher des Pénitents, Les Mées

new.title: Raft the Ubaye river from Barcelonnette
new.desc: Montagnes d'Ubaye runs family and sport rafting on the Ubaye from Barcelonnette; adults pay about 50 euros. Other operators offer half-day trips with class III to IV rapids.
new.tip: Meet in Barcelonnette; swimming ability needed. Best May to September.
new.q: Place Aimé Gassier, Barcelonnette

new.title: Hike up to Lac d'Allos from the Laus car park
new.desc: Lac d'Allos is a high mountain lake in Mercantour, reached by a walk from the Laus car park via stairs cut in the sandstone. The climb takes about 45 minutes.
new.tip: In summer parking at Laus is paid and limited, around 10 euros; ask Allos tourist office.
new.q: Parking du Laus, Allos

new.title: Browse the Monday market in Forcalquier
new.desc: Forcalquier's weekly market takes over Place du Bourguet and the streets around on Monday mornings with up to 200 stallholders selling local produce and crafts. In July and August about fifty extra traders join.
new.tip: Monday 8:00 to 13:00 or 14:00; arrive early to find parking.
new.q: Place du Bourguet, Forcalquier

new.title: Watch the Corso de la Lavande parade in Digne
new.desc: Digne's lavender festival, in its 80th edition in 2026, runs around the first weekend of August with flower floats, concerts and a fair. The Sunday float parade draws thousands.
new.tip: Grandstand seats cost a few euros; watching from the streets is free. 2026: 31 July to 4 August.
new.q: Centre-ville, Digne-les-Bains

new.title: Visit the lavender farm of Lavandes Angelvin
new.desc: Lavandes Angelvin in Valensole offers free visits of its farm during the bloom, roughly 6 to 25 July, with honey for sale. The plateau fields flower from mid-June to mid-July.
new.tip: Reserve by phone or email; early morning has the best light.
new.q: Lavandes Angelvin, Valensole

new.title: Soak in the thermal spa of Digne-les-Bains
new.desc: The spa thermal in Digne uses 50 degree water from the 870 m Ophélia borehole. It has indoor pools, sauna, hammam and fitness room, open all year.
new.tip: Thermal cures run March to October, closed Sundays. Book treatments.
new.q: Thermes de Digne, 29 avenue des Thermes, Digne-les-Bains
